entries.title: Genesis 29:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 Jacob comes to the well of Haran. 9 He becomes acquainted with Rachel. 13 Laban entertains him. 18 Jacob covenants for Rachel. 23 He is deceived by Laban with Leah. 28 He marries also Rachel, and serves for her seven years more. 32 Leah bears Reuben; 33 Simeon; 34 Levi; 35 and Judah.

Jacob. Ps 119:32,60; Ec 9:7 went on his journey. Heb. lifted up his feet. came. 22:20-23; 24:10; 25:20; 28:5-7; Nu 23:7; Jud 6:3,33; 7:12; 8:10 1Ki 4:30; Ho 12:12 people. Heb. children. east.The district of Mesopotamia, and the whole country beyond the Euphrates, are called Kedem, or the East, in the Sacred Writings.

entries.title: Genesis 29:2
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: a well. 24:11,13; Ex 2:15,16; Joh 4:6,14 there. Ps 23:2; So 1:6,7; Isa 49:10; Re 7:17 a great stone.In Arabia, and other places in the East, they cover up their wells of water, lest the sand, which is put in motion by the winds, should fill and quite stop them up. So great was their care not to leave the well open any length of time, that they waited till the flocks were all gathered together before they began to draw water; and when they had finished, the well was immediately closed again.

entries.title: Genesis 29:3
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: the flocks.Instead of {haadarim,} "the flocks," the Samaritan reads {haroin,} "the shepherds," as does also the Arabic in Walton's Polyglott. This verse describes what was usually done by some mutual compact among the shepherds, and shows the purpose for which the flocks lay by the well; for the stone was not removed till all the flocks had been collected. Scott.

entries.title: Genesis 29:6
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Is he well? Heb. there peace to him? 37:14; 43:27; Ex 18:7; 1Sa 17:22; 25:5; 2Sa 20:9

entries.title: Genesis 29:7
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Lo. Ga 6:9,10; Eph 5:16 it is yet high day. Heb. yet the day is great.

entries.title: Genesis 29:9
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Rachel. 24:15; Ex 2:15,16,21; So 1:7,8 for she kept them.In those primitive times, a pastoral life was not only considered useful but honourable: nor was it beneath the dignity of the daughters of the most opulent chiefs to carry water from the well, or tend the sheep. Jacob, Moses, and David were shepherds.

entries.title: Genesis 29:13
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: tidings. Heb. hearing. he ran. 24:29 kissed. 45:15; Ex 4:27; 18:7; 2Sa 19:39; Lu 7:45; Ac 20:37; Ro 16:16 all these. Col 4:5

entries.title: Genesis 29:14
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: art my. 12,15; 2:23; 13:8; Jud 9:2; 2Sa 5:1; 19:12,13; Mic 7:5; Eph 5:30 the space of a month. Heb. a month of days.

entries.title: Genesis 29:18
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
loved. 20,30 I will serve.In ancient times, it was a custom among many nations to give dowries for their wives; but Jacob, being poor, offered for Rachel seven year's service.

31:41; 34:12; Ex 22:16,17; 2Sa 3:14; Ho 3:2; 12:12

entries.title: Genesis 29:25
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: in the morning. 1Co 3:13 wherefore. 27:35,36; Jud 1:7; Pr 11:31; Mt 7:2,12; Joh 21:17; Re 3:19

entries.title: Genesis 29:28
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: fulfilled her week.The public marriage feast made on this occasion, seems to have formed the regular method of recognising the marriage, and lasted seven days: it would therefore have been improper to have broken off the solemnities to which all the men of the place had been invited (ver. 22) and probably Laban wished to keep the fraud from the public eye. It is perfectly plain that Jacob did not serve seven years more before he got Rachel to wife.

entries.title: Genesis 29:35
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: A.M. 2255. B.C. 1749. called. 35:26; 38:1-30; 43:8,9; 44:18-34; 46:12; 49:8-12; De 33:7; 1Ch 5:2 Mt 1:2 Judah. that is, Praise. left bearing. Heb. stood frombearing. 49:8 That is, for a time; for she had several children afterwards. (See ch. 30:17, etc.).
